title: HuntOutput
description: Output of one Hunt task: zero-or-more findings plus coverage gaps.

evidence_snippet.description: Verbatim code excerpt that demonstrates the flaw.

poc.description: The proof-of-concept the hunter wrote and ran. Everything in here is the hunter's ACCOUNT of what it did — it is evidence, not a verdict. Whether the PoC proved anything is decided in Python by pyhunt.oracle.gate from run_output, and written to the sibling `execution` object.

run_output.description: REQUIRED, and must be the COMPLETE combined stdout+stderr of the observed run, verbatim and unsummarised. The [PYHUNT-OBSERVER] marker lines in it are the only input the execution gate has. Paraphrasing this field, or trimming it to 'the interesting part', destroys the proof.

succeeded.description: YOUR BELIEF about whether the exploit worked, based on the PoC's own assertions. It does NOT decide the finding's status and it never promotes a finding: pyhunt.oracle.gate re-reads run_output and rules independently. Answer it honestly rather than optimistically — a claim the evidence does not support is logged as an over-claim, which is how prompt drift is detected.

hedged_language.description: Set true if the description uses 'might'/'could'/'possibly' — flags noise for triage.

needs_poc.description: Set true when execution was not available (execution_available=false, or the toolchain was missing) so this finding rests on a static source->sink argument. Do NOT set it to mean 'my PoC did not work' — the execution gate records that outcome itself, and it never deletes a finding.

execution.description: COMPUTED BY PYHUNT — never emit this field. Any value supplied here is overwritten by the execution gate. Documented so the shape is visible to anyone reading the schema.

proven.description: True only for outcome=proven. The single field that means 'confirmed by execution'.

evidence.description: The marker lines that carried the decision.

gaps_observed.description: Areas the hunter could not fully examine — feeds Gapfill.
